claims.text: Introducing a secondary phase into single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloys can overcome their coercivity limitation.
The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is the introduction of a secondary phase.
The proposed intervention will create a dual-phase microstructure.
A dual-phase fcc-hcp high-entropy alloy can undergo strain-induced martensitic transformation of its initial fcc phase.
Transformation-induced plasticity and strain-induced martensitic transformation will cause an increase in coercivity.
The intervention will raise the coercive field above 100 Oe.
The intervention will maintain high saturation magnetization.
The single-phase fcc FeCoNi baseline has a coercive field no greater than 100 Oe.
Increasing the volume fraction of a secondary L12 phase and its lattice misfit can slightly increase coercivity in Al-doped high-entropy alloys.
A VEC range of 6.87 to 8 favors a dual-phase solid solution.
The relevant conditions are room temperature and no external magnetic field.
The exact composition and processing conditions needed to obtain the desired dual-phase microstructure are uncertain.
A controlled series should compare single-phase fcc and dual-phase fcc-hcp FeCoNi-based alloys made using varied compositions and processing conditions.
Coercive field and saturation magnetization will be measured.
The hypothesis is falsified if adding a secondary phase fails to produce coercivity above 100 Oe while maintaining high saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The stated condition of no external magnetic field is incompatible with standard coercive-field and saturation-magnetization measurements, which require an applied and swept magnetic field.
